## Circles to Spheres ### From the Circle $S^1$ to the Sphere $S^2$ via Quaternions The primitive oscillator lives on the unit circle $S^1 \subset \mathbb{C}$: $$ z(\theta) \;=\; e^{i\theta}, \quad \theta \in [0,2\pi). $$ This representation captures the **binary polarity** (+/−) and its continuous extension as a phase. To lift this system into a higher-dimensional setting, use the **quaternions**: $$ \mathbb{H} = \{\, a + b\,\mathbf{i} + c\,\mathbf{j} + d\,\mathbf{k} \;:\; a,b,c,d \in \mathbb{R} \,\}, $$ with multiplication rules $\mathbf{i}^2 = \mathbf{j}^2 = \mathbf{k}^2 = \mathbf{ijk} = -1$. --- #### Quaternionic Embedding of $S^1$ The circle element $e^{i\theta}$ embeds into the unit quaternions $S^3 \subset \mathbb{H}$ as $$ q(\theta) = \cos\theta \;+\; \sin\theta \,\mathbf{i}. $$ This is still a 1-parameter subgroup, but now it lives inside a 3-sphere. --- #### The Hopf Map: $S^3 \to S^2$ Unit quaternions act on $\mathbb{R}^3$ by conjugation: $$ \mathbf{v} \;\mapsto\; q \,\mathbf{v}\, q^{-1}, \quad \mathbf{v} \in \text{Im}(\mathbb{H}) \cong \mathbb{R}^3. $$ This defines the **Hopf fibration**, a projection from $S^3$ to $S^2$. Explicitly, the map $$ h: (z_1,z_2) \in \mathbb{C}^2,\ |z_1|^2+|z_2|^2=1 \;\mapsto\; \bigl(2\Re(z_1 \bar z_2),\; 2\Im(z_1 \bar z_2),\; |z_1|^2 - |z_2|^2 \bigr) $$ sends points on $S^3$ to points on $S^2$.
